verdict.rationale: Conductor's core documented function is running coding agents (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, OpenCode) on your codebase. You can send prompts to them, start a workspace from a GitHub or Linear issue, and review the resulting diff and PR. The actual plain-language-to-code implementation comes from those bundled third-party agents, and the evidence never explicitly shows multi-file feature or bug implementation. Missing for 10: explicit documentation of plain-language feature or bug fixes spanning multiple files, Conductor-native code-generation capability independent of third-party agents, and hands-on corroboration of multi-file edits.

support.subject: As a developer, I can describe a feature or bug in plain language and have the agent implement or fix it across multiple files

citations.quote: Conductor is a Mac app that lets you run many coding agents in parallel on your codebase.
Create workspaces, send prompts to the coding agent, and read its replies.
create a workspace from a branch, pull request, GitHub issue, or Linear issue
When the work is ready, Conductor helps you review the diff, open a pull request, merge, and archive the workspace.
